 What changes in France 
 On the Agenda: What’s happening in France this week
 James Harrington - news@thelocal.fr
 Published: 1 Nov, 2026 CET. 
 Updated: Sun 1 Nov 2026 08:09 CET 
 Share 
 Add a comment 
 Another day of protests are planned on Thursday. (Photo by DAMIEN MEYER / AFP) 
 Add The Local as a preferred source 
 Children head back to – possibly blockaded – schools after the Toussaint holidays, a long-planned nationwide strike takes place, France’s newest motorway is set to open, and the winner of a major literature award is announced
 Monday 
 Back to school – Millions of school-age children across France head back to classes after the Toussaint holiday break. The next school holiday – apart from the Armistice Day public holiday on Wednesday, November 11th – is the Christmas vacation, which starts after classes on December 18th.  
 READ ALSO How to plan your holidays - and 'ponts' - in France in 2026/27 
 Space – French astronaut Sophie Adenot, who spent nearly eight months on the ISS, will speak at a press conference in Paris, less than a month after returning to Earth with Crew-12. 
 READ ALSO ISS to host first spacewalk by Frenchwoman 
 Court – The money laundering and tax evasion trial of three companies and 14 people, including a Belgian prince in relation to the so-called Dubai Papers begins. 
 Find out what's changing in France with our weekly and monthly outlook
 Sign up 
 Sport – The ninth and final ATP Masters 1000 event of the tennis season, the Paris Masters, gets under way at Plenitude Arena, in the Paris suburbs. 
 Tuesday 
 Protest – With schools back, the lycée students protests restart, with calls for more blockades on Tuesday.  Students in Paris also plan a demonstration starting at Place du Panthéon and heading to Medef headquarters on Avenue Bosquet (although it's not certain whether the demo route will be authorised).  
 Award – the winner of France’s most prestigious literary award, the Prix Goncourt, will be announced at 12 noon. The four shortlisted authors are Yannick Haenel, for La solitude des professeurs est infinie ; Philippe Jaenada, for L’inconnue du Quai de Javel ; Clémentine Mélois, for Choses que je croyais perdues ; and Sylvain Prudhomme, for De l’autre côté du lac . 
 Culture – The 80th Anniversary of the founding of Unesco will be marked in Paris. 
 Advertisement
 Thursday 
 National strike – After a month of various protests involving lycée students, and the return of the Gilet Jaune movement, French unions have called for a day of cross-sector strikes and demos on November 5th, with unions calling on workers, retirees and young people to take to the streets. 
 The strike is in protest at cost-cutting measures in the budget, and will likely result in disruption to public transport and other services. Find the latest here . 
 Taxes – Second home owners in France will receive taxe d’habitation bills between November 5th and 26th. The deadline for payment is between December 15th and 28th, depending on how you pay . 
 Friday   
 Autoroute – France’s newest autoroute, the controversial A69 connecting Toulouse and Castres, is due to open 
 READ ALSO A69: France's newest motorway (finally) set to open 
 Advertisement
 Football – National football team manager Zinedine Zidane will unveil Les Bleus squad for the Nations League matches against Italy and Turkey. 
 Saturday 
 Rugby union – France’s men’s senior national side face Fiji in Lyon in the first match of four in the November leg of the Nations Championship.
